name: H.O.P.E
description: H.O.P.E is a self-hosted server and network observatory: a Rust server with a SQLite database discovers the LAN (ARP, ping and port probes), receives reports from signed Rust agents (CPU, memory with cache and ZFS ARC, load, disks and pools, I/O, bandwidth, temperatures, systemd units, network monitors) and serves a static console with a network map and per-host history. This script installs the prebuilt server and console from the project's GitHub releases; update installs the newest build.

notes.text: The console is served over HTTPS by Caddy with an internal CA; accept the certificate in the browser. The first-run setup token is HOPE_SETUP_TOKEN in /etc/hope/hope.env and stays valid until the first account exists.
Agents must trust the same CA: copy /etc/hope/ca.crt from the container to /etc/hope/ca.crt on every agent host before running the generated install command.
Agent packages are signed with this container's own key, /etc/hope/release-signing.pem, which updates reuse. Back it up: agents installed from this server only accept releases signed with it.
Layer-2 discovery sees only the container's own bridge network; put the container on the VLAN or bridge you want to observe.
